game_title: CATAN – Le Jeu de Base (Livret de règles)
edition_notes: © 1995, 2025 KOSMOS Verlag; French edition distributed by Asmodee France (adaptation Edge Studio); 2025 edition with 4 player colors (white, orange, red, blue)

items.rule: Assemble the frame pieces and place the 19 terrain tiles (1 desert and 5 other terrain types) inside the frame, either as in the beginner layout diagram or, for the expert setup, shuffled face down and placed randomly then flipped face up.
Each terrain produces one resource: Hills produce Clay, Forest produces Wood, Pasture produces Wool, Fields produce Grain, Mountains produce Ore; the Desert produces nothing.

Place the number tokens on the terrain tiles (beginner: as in the diagram; expert: tokens A onward placed in alphabetical order in a counter-clockwise spiral toward the center, starting at a corner tile, then flipped to show numbers). The Desert gets no number token and is skipped.
Place the Robber pawn on the Desert tile.
Each player chooses a color and takes the matching pieces: 5 settlements, 4 cities and 15 roads. With 3 players, the white pieces are returned to the box.
Sort the resource cards by type into 5 face-up piles in the trays; shuffle the Development cards and put them face down in the last compartment. The trays form the Supply (Réserve) next to the board.
Each player takes a Building Costs card; the Longest Road and Largest Army special cards and the 2 dice are placed next to the board.

Expert setup placement phase: each player rolls the dice, the highest total goes first. In the 1st round, in clockwise order, each player places 1 settlement on any free intersection and connects 1 road to one of its 3 adjacent paths, respecting the Distance Rule.
In the 2nd placement round, the last player to place begins and play proceeds counter-clockwise: each player places a 2nd settlement (respecting the Distance Rule) and connects 1 road to it.
Starting resources: each player takes from the Supply 1 resource card for each terrain tile adjacent to their (second, in expert setup) settlement and keeps them hidden in hand.

Beginner setup: each player starts with 2 settlements and 2 roads already placed on the island as in the diagram (keeping 3 settlements, 13 roads and 4 cities in front of them); the first player is the one with the highest total on a roll of both dice.
Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, do in order: 1) Resource phase (roll the dice), 2) Trade and Build phase. Then pass the dice to the left neighbor.

Roll both dice and add them. If the total is not 7, every player with a settlement adjacent to a terrain tile whose number token matches the total receives 1 resource card of that terrain's type; each city gives 2 cards. Multiple buildings each produce separately.
If a 7 is rolled, no terrain produces. Every player with more than 7 resource cards must return half of them (their choice) to the Supply, rounding down (e.g. 9 cards → return 4).
On a 7, the active player must move the Robber to a different terrain tile and steals 1 random resource card from the hand of another player who has a settlement or city adjacent to that tile.
A terrain tile occupied by the Robber does not produce resources when its number is rolled: owners of adjacent settlements/cities receive nothing.
In the Trade and Build phase, the active player may trade, build and buy Development cards in any order and any number of times, or do nothing.
Trading with players: you may trade resource cards with any other player by negotiating; other players may only trade with the active player, not among themselves.
Trading with the Supply is 4:1: return 4 identical resource cards and take 1 resource card of a different type of your choice.

Harbors: with a settlement or city on a harbor intersection, a generic harbor lets you trade 3:1 (3 identical cards for 1 of your choice); a specialized harbor lets you trade 2:1 only for the resource shown (2 cards of that type for 1 of your choice).

Road costs 1 Clay + 1 Wood. Roads are built only on paths (edges between tiles or tile and sea), 1 road per path, and must connect to one of your settlements/cities or to an unoccupied intersection extending one of your roads.

Settlement costs 1 Clay + 1 Wood + 1 Wool + 1 Grain. It must be built on an intersection reached by at least one of your roads and obey the Distance Rule: all 3 adjacent intersections must be unoccupied by any settlement or city.
City costs 2 Grain + 3 Ore. It can only be built by upgrading one of your settlements already on the board; the settlement returns to your personal supply.
Development card costs 1 Wool + 1 Grain + 1 Ore: draw the top card, look at it and keep it face down in front of you. Spent resource cards go back to the Supply.
You may play only 1 Development card per turn (at any time, even before rolling the dice), and cannot play a card bought during the same turn. Each card can be played only once.
Knight card: move the Robber to another terrain tile and steal 1 resource card from a player adjacent to it, as for a 7; the played Knight stays face up in front of you.

Monopoly: name 1 resource type; all other players must give you all cards of that type from their hand. Road Building: build 2 roads for free. Year of Plenty (Invention): take any 2 resource cards from the Supply. Played cards are placed face up.
Each settlement is worth 1 victory point and each city is worth 2 victory points.

Longest Road card (2 VP): given to the first player with a continuous road of at least 5 road pieces (branches not counted) not interrupted by an opponent's settlement or city; another player takes it immediately by building a strictly longer road.
Largest Army card (2 VP): given to the first player with 3 played Knight cards face up; another player takes it immediately by having more Knight cards than the current holder.
Victory Point Development cards each give 1 VP; they are kept face down and only revealed if they bring you to 10 points on your turn (several can be revealed, including ones just bought).
The game ends when the active player reaches 10 or more victory points during their turn.
The first player to reach 10 victory points (on their own turn) is declared the winner immediately.
Expert setup variant: shuffle the terrain tiles and place randomly, place number tokens in alphabetical spiral order instead of using the beginner layout, and use the 2-round placement phase.
